question: $20\ \text{g}$ of NaOH (molar mass $40\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$) is dissolved in water to make $100\ \text{mL}$ of solution. Find its molarity.

question: The molar solubility of $\text{CaF}_2$ is $s = 10^{-3}\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$. Calculate its solubility product $K_{sp}$.
anchor: $\text{CaF}_2 \rightleftharpoons \text{Ca}^{2+} + 2\text{F}^-$, so $K_{sp} = s(2s)^2 = 4s^3$.
why: $\text{CaF}_2 \rightleftharpoons \text{Ca}^{2+} + 2\text{F}^-$, so $K_{sp} = s(2s)^2 = 4s^3$. $K_{sp} = 4s^3 = 4\times(10^{-3})^3$ $K_{sp} = 4\times10^{-9}\ \text{mol}^3\text{L}^{-3}$

why: $\Delta H^\circ = \sum\Delta H_f(\text{products}) - \sum\Delta H_f(\text{reactants})$. $\Delta H^\circ = (-286) + (-242) - (-200)$ $\Delta H^\circ = -328\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
